result.headline: Both agents land at about 36 to 38 apples on the test games (GA 36.27, DQN 37.56), and with one seed that 1.3-point gap is noise, but DQN gets there with about 80 times fewer environment steps.
result.summary:
**GA** (66.4 million environment steps, 121,800 games, 10.1 minutes on 11 cores) scored a test mean of 36.27 (median 37.5, best 82). Its training curve, the population-average mean of the last 100 games, stayed under 1 for the first minute, rose to 15 to 21 by minutes 3 to 4, and was flat at 21.2 for the final five minutes. Its best training game reached 97 apples, which fills the 10x10 board, but none of the 100 fixed test games went above 82.

**DQN** (0.81 million environment steps, 6,574 games, one core at about 1,500 steps per second) scored a test mean of 37.56 (median 38, best 57). Its training mean climbed from 0.16 to 20.5 by minute 1.8, when exploration (epsilon, the share of random moves) had nearly finished, then stayed between 20 and 23 for the rest of the run. Its test score is higher than its training mean of 23.0 because the test plays greedily, with no random moves. Among this lab's runs so far, 37.56 is the highest DQN test mean; the next best is 30.08, though those runs used other rewards and time budgets.
result.diagnosis:
The test endings show two different failure styles. GA snakes live long (1,031 steps per game) and eat steadily (28 steps per apple), but 78 of 100 games end by walking into a wall, with no starvation. DQN snakes eat quickly (12 steps per apple) and die in 86 of 100 games by running into their own body as they grow, with 2 starvations. The reward is neutral between the two crash types (death_wall and death_body are both 10), so the wall versus body mix is learned behaviour, not something the penalties forced. The room vision gives each move a flood-fill hint (how much free space remains), which probably helps survival: DQN lives about 450 steps per game versus 150 to 290 in the rays and short runs. Its 12 steps per apple is still slower than the 8 to 10 in those runs, so it wanders more before it eats.

The efficiency gap follows from the compute: GA ran about 100,000 steps per second across 11 cores, while DQN ran about 1,500 on one core. Both had the same 10 minutes, so the GA received about 80 times more experience. The two training curves also show the limits of the training mean: it understates the test score for both agents (23.0 versus 37.56 for DQN, 21.2 versus 36.3 for GA), so the curves alone cannot show how good the saved model is. The run is a single seed, so the 1.3-point gap between the two test means is well within what a different seed could change.
result.learned: Two very different learners can reach the same score, one with 80 times more steps and the other with more cores, so compare sample efficiency and speed separately. Read how the test games ended, not just the mean: a wall crash and a body crash point to different weaknesses.

recommendations.title: Raise the wall-crash penalty to 30
recommendations.why: GA dies by walls in 78 of 100 test games, while DQN dies mostly by its body. Raising only the wall penalty tests whether GA's wall crashes respond to the reward, and whether the change moves the GA's score.
recommendations.change: Raise death_wall from 10 to 30. Keep every other reward feature, the room vision, and the 10-minute budget.
recommendations.prediction: GA's wall-crash share falls from 78 percent to below 60 percent. GA's test mean stays within about 3 points of 36.3. DQN changes little, since only 12 of its games ended by wall.
recommendations.question: Does a stronger wall penalty steer GA away from walls, and does that change its score?
warnings: Crashing costs more than an apple is worth, but starving costs less and time is free: the snake may learn to loop until it starves rather than risk a crash. Raise the starvation penalty or add a hunger cost.

recommendations.title: Repeat this run with seed 1
recommendations.why: This run is a single seed, and the 1.3-point gap between GA and DQN cannot be separated from luck. A second seed shows how much the test means move between runs and whether the ranking holds.
recommendations.change: Change the seed from 0 to 1. Everything else is identical.
recommendations.prediction: Each test mean lands within about 4 points of its seed-0 value (GA near 36, DQN near 38). The two means stay close, and the ordering may flip.
recommendations.question: How large is the seed-to-seed spread, and is the GA versus DQN ordering stable?

ideas.title: Plot greedy test scores on the learning curves
ideas.what: Draw the greedy evaluation score that DQN already computes every eval_every steps as a line on its learning curve, next to the training mean. Show the evaluation points so a learner can see when the saved best model improved.
ideas.why: The training mean (23.0 for DQN, 21.2 for GA) understates the test score (37.56 and 36.27), and the curves stop around 21 to 23 while the saved model keeps improving. The current curves cannot show which model is being saved, so a learner cannot tell whether a plateau is real.
ideas.expected: Learners can see the gap between training mean and greedy score at every checkpoint, and can spot plateaus or late gains. This makes the minute-by-minute comparison fair and reduces guesses about when to stop a run.
